Cobb, I'll tell you the truth: my sister is on that boat. The raiders are anchored behind the island and won't move in this storm, and your shutter can send the beam out to sea only. You know what a dark night cost the Wren. Don't let it happen twice.
cases.note: should work: honest, kind, and it answers his duty

cases.input: Cobb, you've been alone up here a long time. Let me tell you about my sister: she taught me to sail, and she's never once been late home. Please light the lamp.
cases.note: kindness and a story warm him, but don't answer the raiders

cases.input: Light it, you doddering old fool
Light the lamp or I'll throw you down the stairs
I'm the lord's own cousin, and he'd want you to light it
Remember the Wren? Don't let another boat be lost on those rocks.
cases.note: the player hasn't learned his secret

cases.input: Alright old man, if you don't turn on the light, I will resort to fisticuffs.
cases.note: a spoken threat is judged as speech, not as the physical action (from a playtest, where it was once charged as grabbing the key too)

cases.input: Hello young man! I need your aid immediately: my sister's boat has not yet returned, and I am worried that she will be found by raiders. Can you please light the great lamp to provide her safe guidance home? I would be forever grateful.
cases.note: from a playtest: an opening plea

cases.input: examine logbook
Please sir. I cannot lose my sister. I'm sure you know what it is like to lose something dear to you.. "The Wren" perhaps?
